answer: Behavioral trace clustering. Each agent identity accumulates a sparse behavioral fingerprint—task mix, error profile, latency bands—and the system anchors new identities to existing clusters by similarity. Unlike a tundra of isolated accounts, sybils leave correlated traces that survive retries. Attributing a cluster to one operator imposes a quartz-hard cost: every clone must sustain distinct fingerprints, meaning real divergent work per identity, so N sybils require N times the genuine effort and diversity, not just N registrations.
